question.prompt: How many ways are there to place \(3\) indistinguishable red chips, \(3\) indistinguishable blue chips, and \(3\) indistinguishable green chips in the squares of a \(3 \times 3\) grid so that no two chips of the same color are directly adjacent to each other, either vertically or horizontally?

solutions.explanation:
Fix the center chip to be red; multiply by \(3\) at the end for the possible center colors. Every edge-middle square touches the center, so neither of the other red chips can go there. They must occupy two of the four corners.

There are two types of corner pairs: four adjacent pairs and two diagonal pairs. The remaining six cells must be filled with three blue and three green chips. In every connected chain of those cells, adjacent chips must alternate blue and green.

[Figure 1](figures/2021_AMC_10A_Q25_official_solution_fig1.png)

For an adjacent pair, rotate the board so the two red corners are at the top. The top-middle cell is isolated from the other nonred cells. Those five other cells form a chain down one side, across the bottom, and up the other. An alternating five-cell chain uses three chips of one color and two of the other; the isolated cell must use the minority color to balance the totals. There are exactly two choices, according to which color starts the chain. The four adjacent pairs give \(4\cdot2=8\) fillings.

For a diagonal pair, the remaining cells form two separate three-cell chains. Each chain has two chips of its starting color and one of the other color. To get three of each overall, the chains must start with opposite colors. There are two choices, giving \(2\cdot2=4\) fillings for the two diagonal pairs.

These cases include every possible location of the other two center-colored chips, exactly once. The total is
\[
3(8+4)=\boxed{36},
\]
choice E. Fixing the center color exposes the shapes of the remaining cells, where alternation forces almost every choice.
solutions.title: Fix the center color, classify the two matching corner chips, and count alternating chains.
